conversations.name: White-haired old man
pages:
When you sit here, the footsteps reach you first.
I could hear you a little while before you arrived.

Even people in a hurry take smaller steps here.
Perhaps it is the long bridges. Perhaps it is what is on their minds.

Thank you for talking to me.
Next time, I might know it is you just by your footsteps.

conversations.name: Thin woman
pages:
You can go ahead of me.
These are the biggest steps I can manage right now.

When I look into the distance, my heart gets tired before my legs do.
So I take the stones at my feet one at a time.

I have made it one stone farther than before.
...I think I will call that enough.

conversations.name: Motionless young man
pages:
I stopped because I was going to turn right.
Then I started thinking left might be just as good.

I suppose it is less about which way is right,
and more about not wanting to regret my choice.

You go on ahead.
If I follow someone, I will only get out of choosing for myself again.

conversations.name: Downcast old woman
pages:
From here, I can see the faces of people passing by.
Standing up to wait has become too much for me.

I do not know whom I am waiting for.
But I cannot say for certain that it is not you.

If you happen to come this way again...
Would you please not introduce yourself as a stranger?

conversations.name: Little girl
pages:
Look, this crack is like a river.
You can see it if you crouch down. There, the narrow bit.

This is a house, and this is a bridge.
It is not a real map, so it is all right if you get lost.

Can I make a place for you too?
On this side, where you do not have to cross the river.

conversations.name: Boy with his head down
pages:
One, two, three...
Oh. When you spoke to me, I forgot where I was.

You do not have to say sorry. I was only counting my steps.
It is not as if I get anything when I finish.

Maybe I will start from ten next time.
It is cheating, but a little bit should be all right.

conversations.name: Tired man
pages:
I thought I might see the edge if I went up high enough.
Even after I came down the stairs, my legs still felt as if they were climbing.

What I saw was another tower, and another beyond it.
I could see more of the world. I did not find any more answers.

I do not feel like going anywhere high just now.
Let me walk on level ground for a little while.

conversations.name: Pensive woman
pages:
Could you stay there a moment?
I am listening to the silence just after someone has spoken.

It is different from the silence when you are alone, is it not?
...It sounds a little different to me.

That is enough now.
I will remember the place where your voice was a little longer.

conversations.name: Man watching the grass
pages:
From down here, you can see the gaps between the stones.
They look empty, but sometimes a thin blade of grass is still there.

I cannot tell whether it has grown.
Watch for long enough, and you forget what it looked like before.

Even standing up to check feels like too much trouble.
For today, finding it will have to do.

conversations.name: Old man waiting for the lights
pages:
The lights do not all come on at once in the evening, do they?
I stand here and watch to see which will be first.

Remembering yesterday's order never helps me guess.
It is as if someone thinks it over afresh every time.

Just waiting turns into a guessing game.
It wears out my legs, but it is not a bad way to pass the time.

conversations.name: Woman with slumped shoulders
pages:
Today, I tried starting with my left foot.
Not that I expect it to change anything.

I have grown a little tired of doing the same things.
I still do not have the energy for a big change.

Oh, which foot was that just now?
Even something so small gives me more to think about.

conversations.name: Old woman hugging her knees
pages:
Sometimes, when I rest my hands on my knees, my fingers move.
As if I were sewing something. Though I have no needle.

Was I mending someone's clothes?
The more I think about it, the more my fingers fall still.

I have decided not to tell myself to remember.
I will keep whatever my hands still know.

conversations.name: Boy waiting for the moon
pages:
How does the moon come back after it sets over there?
Is there a bridge underneath too?

I thought I would find out if I watched, so I stood here all this time.
But once it was out of sight, it just stayed out of sight.

...Even looking up has made me tired.
Will you tell me when it comes out again?

conversations.name: Old man with a limp
pages:
I hated going back the way I had come. It felt like losing.
So I took some very long ways round.

Now, if I want to go back, I turn around.
Making a road into something to win or lose only tires your feet.

The trouble is, once I turn around, I forget
which way I wanted to go a moment ago.

conversations.name: Woman resting her hands on her knees
pages:
Just looking for somewhere to sit wore me out.
In the end, I sat down where I had first stopped.

I am sure there are better places.
But surely I am allowed a reason to stay here too.

The space beside me is free.
You can decide for yourself whether it feels like somewhere to settle.

conversations.name: Man making way
pages:
Can you get through?
Stand around daydreaming, and you end up blocking someone else's path.

I do not know the roads well enough to give directions.
And I cannot carry your bags. You have none either.

At least I can try not to keep you too long.
Take care. ...Yes, that much I can say for now.

conversations.name: Girl trudging along
pages:
When someone asks me to walk with them,
I start thinking I have to walk faster.

Maybe they would be happy to wait for me.
But making someone wait is tiring too.

You can go ahead.
Please do not be angry if I never catch up.

conversations.name: Man resting his arms on his knees
pages:
I was thinking of opening an inn here.
No chairs or beds, but the view is excellent.

The price of a room is one good story.
...No need to look so troubled. I am joking.

With an innkeeper like this, it will never open.
I sat down before I even put up the sign.

conversations.name: Old woman with narrowed eyes
pages:
Have you seen anything unusual today?
I have been standing here for quite some time.

It need not be a great discovery.
A chipped stone, perhaps, or a strangely shaped blade of grass.

I can listen to stories like that.
I have already heard so many times that there is no way out.

conversations.name: Slow-walking woman
pages:
My feet stop when someone speaks to me.
I thought I was still walking.

I wanted to say something to the last person I met,
but the words only came after we parted. I am always too late.

I might think of an answer for you later too.
If we meet again, will you hear the rest?
